clauses.current_legal_basis: The U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints Executive Order 12234 in full, with no amendment notation, as a note to 33 U.S.C. 1602, and the eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (46 CFR 31.40-45, 91.60-45, 189.60-45) still applies the order and the 1974 Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea.
clauses.reason: Section 1-101 records that the 1974 Convention, signed November 1, 1974 and proclaimed January 28, 1980, entered into force for the United States on May 25, 1980. It is a declaration on which sections 1-102 to 1-105 operate, and nothing held shows the Convention ceased to bind the United States; the eCFR provisions held for this claim still implement it as of 2026. The clause is operative, with the Code note as its current basis.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints Executive Order 12234 in full, with no amendment notation, as a note to 33 U.S.C. 1602, and the eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (46 CFR 31.40-45, 91.60-45, 189.60-45) still applies the order and the 1974 Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea.
clauses.reason: Section 1-102 directs the Secretary of State, the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard operates, the Secretary of Commerce and the Federal Communications Commission to perform the Convention functions within their areas and to cooperate. No later order or statute held ends or amends the direction; the Code note prints it unamended. EO 13286 (2003) changed the Coast Guard's department by statute and order elsewhere, but the clause already refers to the department in which the Coast Guard is operating, so no amendment of this clause was needed or made.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The eCFR text of 46 CFR 31.40-45(a) designates the American Bureau of Shipping to issue the Cargo Ship Safety Construction Certificate on behalf of the United States under Regulation 12, chapter I of the 1974 Convention and Executive Order 12234, in effect until terminated by proper authority; 46 CFR 91.60-45 and 189.60-45 do the same for other vessel classes.
clauses.reason: Section 1-103(a) makes the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard operates, or another authorized agency head, responsible for issuing certificates required by the Convention. The held eCFR sections show the Coast Guard still issuing and delegating certificate authority on the basis of this order as of 2026. The clause is operative.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints Executive Order 12234 in full, with no amendment notation, as a note to 33 U.S.C. 1602, and the eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (46 CFR 31.40-45, 91.60-45, 189.60-45) still applies the order and the 1974 Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea.
clauses.reason: Section 1-103(b) requires an issuing agency to ascertain the decision of the agency that holds the relevant statutory function and makes that decision final and binding on the issuing agency. It is a standing rule of procedure with no end of its own, and the Code note prints it unamended. The clause is operative.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The eCFR text of 46 CFR 31.40-45(a) designates the American Bureau of Shipping under Executive Order 12234, and states the designation is in effect until terminated by proper authority and notice published in the Federal Register; the Code note prints section 1-104 unamended.
clauses.reason: Section 1-104 allows the Secretary to use the American Bureau of Shipping, while it is operated in compliance with the 1920 Act provision cited there, and the National Cargo Bureau for grain carriage. The held eCFR sections show continued reliance on the American Bureau of Shipping as of 2026. The National Cargo Bureau permission is a discretionary authority whose current basis is the unamended Code note only; no held source shows its use or withdrawal. The clause is operative.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The eCFR text of 46 CFR 189.60-45, 31.40-45 and 91.60-45 are regulations of the Coast Guard that cite Executive Order 12234 as their basis for certificate issuance under the Convention (eCFR as of 2026-10-14).
clauses.reason: Section 1-105 directs the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard operates to promulgate regulations necessary to implement the Convention. The held eCFR sections are such regulations and remain in force as of 2026, which shows the direction has not been withdrawn. The clause is operative.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints Executive Order 12234 in full, with no amendment notation, as a note to 33 U.S.C. 1602, and the eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (46 CFR 31.40-45, 91.60-45, 189.60-45) still applies the order and the 1974 Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea.
clauses.reason: Section 1-106 supersedes EO 11239 of July 31, 1965 to the extent the 1974 Convention replaces and abrogates the 1960 Convention. It operates as a continuing limit on EO 11239 rather than a completed act, and EO 13286 section 65 (effective March 1, 2003) amended EO 11239 expressly without prejudice to section 1-106. That order is a recital of this clause and does not amend or end it. The clause is operative.

Section 1-107 states that Executive Order 10402 of October 30, 1952 is revoked. The order contains no later effective date, so the revocation took effect when the order was signed on September 3, 1980. The command was fully performed by that act; it requires no continuing performance, and the held Code note to 33 U.S.C. 143 treats EO 10402 as ended. The first end of this clause is therefore September 3, 1980, by performance of the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12234 of September 3, 1980 (45 FR 58801) was read in full from the held Federal Register original (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12234.txt, PDF page 9). Its heading and number match the register and the 1989 codification, and the signing date is September 3, 1980. It has seven numbered sections (1-101 to 1-107, with 1-103 divided into (a) and (b)); the inventory matches that text. The order has no sunset, expiry or revocation of its own. Current law: the U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints the order in full, with no amendment notation, as a note to 33 U.S.C. 1602, and the held eCFR text of 46 CFR 31.40-45, 91.60-45 and 189.60-45 designates the American Bureau of Shipping to issue certificates under the 1974 Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea and Executive Order 12234. No Federal Register catalog disposition note names this order as amended, revoked or superseded. The only later order in the held corpus that cites it by number is EO 13286 (68 FR 10619, effective March 1, 2003), whose section 65 amends EO 11239 without prejudice to section 1-106 of EO 12234; that is a recital and does not amend, revoke or supersede EO 12234. Bounded searches read for coverage before use: current-law:usc covers the U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted after that date and on or before 2026-10-14 are not reflected); current-law:ecfr covers the eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML; later-events:ofr_catalog covers Office of the Federal Register disposition notes of 6942 catalog records (1937 onward) plus operative sentences in 16784 saved order texts. These are machine leads, not independent review; the two-week gap in the U.S. Code edition is disclosed here.

savings.reason: The held text contains no savings, transition or pending-action clause. The only provisions that act on other instruments are 1-106 (supersession of EO 11239 to the extent stated) and 1-107 (revocation of EO 10402); each is treated in its own clause row, and the held text of 12234 states nothing that preserves actions under EO 10402 or EO 11239.
